div.head: Norðleoda 11
div.ab: And gif his sunu ⁊ his sunu sunu þæt geþeoð, þæt hi swa micel landes habban, siððan bið se ofsprinc gesiðcundes cynnes be twam þusendum.
⁊ gif his sunu ⁊ his suna sunu þæt geþeoð, þæt hy swa micel landes habbað, syððan byþ se ofspring gesiðcundes cynnes be twam ðusendum þrymsa.
⁊ gif his sunu ⁊ þæs sun sunu þæt begyten, þæt he swa micle landes habbaþ, sien hiora æftergengas ðæs siþcunda cynnes, ⁊ gyld ðam mon mid II m. ðrimsa.
Et si filius eius et filius filii eius hoc assequatur, ut tantum terre habeant, postmodum (postea) est qui nascetur ex eis, siþcunde generationis, ad duo milia t[h]rim.
And gif his sunu and his suna sunu þæt geþeoð þæt hy swa micel landes habbað, syððan byþ se offspring gesiðcundes cynnes be twam þusendum þrymsa.

Und wenn sein Sohn und seines (des Ld) Sohnes Sohn dás erreichen, dass sie so viel an Land besitzen, dann ist die Nachkommenschaft (seien ihre Nachkommen Ld) von gefolgschaftsadligem Stande (und entgelte man sie Ld) zu 2000 (Tremissen hlq).

And if his son and his (the, Ld) son's son attain this, that they hold so much land, then the offspring (let their descendants, Ld) are of gesith-born rank (and let them be paid for, Ld) at 2,000 (thrymsas, hlq).
And if his son and his son’s son prosper, so that they have so much land, then the offspring is of gesith-born class, at 2,000 [thrymsas].
And if his son and his son’s son prosper so that they have sufficient land, then the offspring will be of the rank of gesith at two thousand thrymsas.
div.note: ‘geþeon’ is transitive here and in Að 2. Liebermann compares Norðleod 5 and 9.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘And if his son and his son's son prosper, so that they have so much land, then the offspring is of gesith-born class, at 2000 thrymsas.’).; AA: corrected against Rabin p. 14 / 15, October 2026 (was “And if his son and his son’s son prosper so that they have sufficient land, then the offspring will be of the rank of gesith at two thousand thrymsas.”, now “And if his son and his son’s son prosper so that they have sufficient land, then the offspring will be of the rank of gesith at two thousand thrymsas. (expanded letters in italics: gesith)”)
gesith: A rank roughly equivalent to a thane found in Northumbrian legal texts.
